raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

On Model Runner V2, GPU memory keeps growing after startup while load ramps up. The sampler makes an fp32 copy of the `[num_reqs, vocab]` logits on every step. `capture_model()` ends with `empty_cache()`, so serving starts with no cached block of that size, and each new largest batch reserves a slightly bigger block while the smaller ones stay cached.

V1 already avoids this: `compile_or_warm_up_model` runs the sampler once at the largest batch *after* `capture_model()` ("on purpose to prevent memory buffers from being cleared by `torch.accelerator.empty_cache`"). This PR adds the same step for MRV2.

**Depends on #57926.** That PR makes `_dummy_sampler_run` take the fp32 path and counts it in `profile_run`. Without it, the dummy run skips the copy and this warm-up keeps nothing.

## Claims

- Memory no longer grows step by step under load (Qwen3-4B: +1.77 GB in 18 steps to +0.11 GB in 1 step; Gemma-4-31B TP4: +0.24 to +0.003 GB per GPU).
- No KV cache cost on top of #57926.
- No throughput change.

## Validation

**Qwen3-4B, TP1, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`**

| | main | #57926 | #57926 + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| KV cache (tokens) | 106,912 | 105,680 | 105,680 |
| Memory growth under load | +1.78 GB (18 steps) | +1.77 GB (18 steps) | +0.11 GB (1 step) |
| Peak GPU memory under load | 25.72 GB | 25.54 GB | 24.11 GB |
| Output tok/s, c=16 / 64 / 160 / 256 | 608 / 1279 / 1562 / 1519 | 607 / 1277 / 1563 / 1503 | 608 / 1276 / 1561 / 1499 |

**Gemma-4-31B-it, TP4, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --kv-cache-memory 3GB`**

| | #57926 | #57926 + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| KV cache (tokens) | 18,806 | 18,806 |
| Memory growth under load (each GPU) | +0.24 GB (3 steps) | +0.003 GB |
| Output tok/s, c=8 / 32 / 64 / 128 | 133 / 496 / 520 / 536 | 133 / 496 / 521 / 537 |

Setup:
- Hardware and software: AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, 32 GB), ROCm 10.1, torch 2.13, vLLM `8a6c0449b3` with #57926 and this PR.


Run on `main`, #57926 and #57926 + this PR. Requests carry no sampling params, so each model's default top-k/top-p applies.

**Qwen3-4B, 1 GPU**

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --port 8000

vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 512 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 1280 --max-concurrency 256 --request-rate inf --seed 1256
```

**Gemma-4-31B, 4 GPUs** (fixed KV size so all builds get the same KV cache)

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-31B-it --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --kv-cache-memory 3221225472 --port 8000

vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model google/gemma-4-31B-it --base-url http://localhost:8000 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 128 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 640 --max-concurrency 128 --request-rate inf --seed 1128
```


## Details

- Not tested on NVIDIA; the code path is the same. I can test on it.

[P1] Use the actual LM-head input dimension for the dummy hidden states

@@ -1228,6 +1228,27 @@ def _compile_or_warm_up_model(self) -> CompilationTimes:
             else:
                 self.model_runner._dummy_sampler_run(hidden_states=last_hidden_states)
 
+        if (
+            self.use_v2_model_runner
+            and get_pp_group().is_last_rank
+            and not self.model_runner.is_pooling_model
+        ):
+            # MRV2 counterpart of the V1 warm-up above: keep the sampler's

+            )
+            self.model_runner._dummy_sampler_run(hidden_states=sample_hidden_states)
+            del sample_hidden_states

inline_comments.body:
AI generated comment:

```bash
[P1] Use the actual LM-head input dimension for the dummy hidden states

model_config.get_hidden_size() is not necessarily the dimension of the final hidden states passed to compute_logits().

For example, facebook/opt-350m has hidden_size=1024 but word_embed_proj_dim=512. OPTDecoder projects its final hidden states to 512 dimensions, and OPTForCausalLM.lm_head expects 512 input features.

This warm-up instead creates a [max_num_reqs, 1024] tensor, so _dummy_sampler_run() calls compute_logits() with an incompatible shape, causing model initialization to fail under MRV2.

Could we derive the dummy tensor shape from the actual final hidden states or the LM head's input dimension instead?
```
